base.probability_evidence: The fact sheet's own blend (DCF base 360.87) and the P/E method (base 437.45) disagree sharply, and the note's 'Unusual items' section finds neither the WSJ interchange-bill headline nor the 10-K litigation disclosure is new information -- both are already reflected in multiples below MA's own 5y range (research/MA/2026-10-09.md section 6) -- so 'price holds near current level absent a confirmed catalyst change' is the single most likely outcome, carrying the majority weight; the macro overlay is only 'secondary' weight (research/MA/2026-10-09-macro.md), so it shifts probability moderately toward bear rather than displacing the base case.

jumps.name: US interchange-fee legislation
jumps.reason: A federal bill restricting interchange fees/routing would directly cut network economics beyond what is already priced into the multiple.
jumps.cite: WSJ 2026-10-08, 'The Credit-Card Bill That Banks Fear Most Has Gained Trump as an Ally' (research/MA/factsheet-2026-10-09.md News & sentiment; research/MA/2026-10-09.md sections 2 and 6); 10-K names interchange-fee regulation/surcharging as Mastercard's top forward-looking risk.

annual_probability.cite: Assumption (no historical analogue): WSJ 2026-10-08 reports the bill has gained political momentum but names no scheduled vote; treated as a low-probability-per-year discrete legislative event given no base-rate data in the 5-year weekly history.

impact.cite: Assumption, bounded well under the montecarlo.max_jump_impact_assumed 0.30 cap: no matching week exists in mc-inputs.json's event/analogue tables for a regulatory shock, so impact is set from the WSJ/10-K severity described (top named risk) rather than a historical move.

jumps.assumption: No discrete regulatory-shock week appears in mc-inputs.json's largest_falls/largest_rises/event_weeks tables (none are tagged as regulatory), so both annual_probability and impact are stated assumptions, with impact kept at or below the 0.30 cap for an unanalogued jump.

jumps.name: Merchant-interchange litigation settlement/judgment
jumps.reason: An adverse settlement or judgment in the long-running US/UK/Netherlands/Portugal merchant-interchange litigation could trigger a one-off charge and sentiment hit distinct from the legislative risk above.
jumps.cite: Mastercard FY2025 10-K (research/MA/2026-10-09.md section 2 and Sources): 'active US, UK, Netherlands and Portugal merchant-interchange litigation dating to 2011'.

annual_probability.cite: Assumption: the 10-K discloses this litigation has been open and unresolved since 2011 (research/MA/2026-10-09.md section 2), roughly 15 years with no settlement yet -- treated as a base rate of about 1-in-15 years for a discrete settlement/judgment event, no historical weekly analogue exists to measure this directly.

impact.cite: Assumption, bounded well under the 0.30 cap: no matching week in mc-inputs.json's analogue tables, and smaller than the legislative-shock jump above because a litigation settlement typically resolves one jurisdiction's exposure rather than the whole US interchange model.

jumps.assumption: No litigation-settlement week appears in mc-inputs.json's analogue tables (event_weeks only tags earnings/proxy/investor-update/M&A types), so annual_probability and impact are stated assumptions, with impact kept well below the 0.30 cap.

jumps.reason: The evaluator's bear case names the Oct 29 print as event risk, and Barron's flags elevated pre-earnings volatility; quarterly earnings reactions are the most frequent discrete catalyst in the stock's own history.

annual_probability.cite: mc-inputs.json analogues.event_weeks: counting the 20 quarterly earnings-release weeks from Q3 2021 to Q2 2026, 2 of 20 (10%) produced a reaction of at least 6.45% magnitude (Q3 2021 -6.45%, Q3 2022 +8.96%); with 4 reports/year at that per-quarter rate, P(at least one such-sized reaction in a year) = 1-(1-0.10)^4 = 0.34.

impact.cite: mc-inputs.json analogues.event_weeks: Q3 2021 earnings release, week 2021-10-25, move -0.0645 -- the largest-magnitude negative earnings-week reaction among MA's quarterly report weeks in the 5-year history.
